selection.why: This plan significantly reduces median case span by 1.6685%, mean case span by 1.7183%, and waiting by 1.5246%, while service (+0.6702%) and utilisation (+4.2063%) remain noise. It is cleaner than the stronger round3c alternative because it removes CA-004, which had no measurable effect.
selection.gain_reading: speed: waiting h/case falls 1.5246% significantly (z=-3.60), while service h/case rises only 0.6702% and is not significant (z=0.13); the same work is therefore moving faster, not being replaced by less work. The payload does not provide absolute waiting or service hours, only these percentage changes and z-values.

selection.runner_up: round3c — it delivered larger measured reductions in median span (-2.5213%), mean span (-2.2213%), and waiting (-1.6393%), but it retained two no-effect passengers, CA-004 and CBW-002.
selection.caveat: Do not over-read the service and utilisation movements: neither is significant. CBW-002 is a passenger and should be removed rather than treated as justified work; the selected plan is preferable because it has fewer such passengers, not because CBW-002 contributes.

compliance_final.note: DECISIONS B: judged on prior knowledge alone and never overturnable by measurement. This ruling decides what the deliverable may contain; measurements of plans it bars are kept under `excluded_as_non_compliant` so the cost of the block can still be read.

note: `best` is the best MEASUREMENT in the run, which is usually not the last round. ⚠️ `statistically_tied_with_best` is the SELECTOR'S CANDIDATE POOL, not a set of indistinguishable results: a row is admitted either because it is not significantly worse than `best` on the median, or because it is decisively better on ONE directional measure while possibly far worse on the others. Read each row's `admitted_because` before describing it, and never call the list a tie. `per_candidate` is the winning plan's own account: what each surviving candidate contributed on waiting, duration, throughput and resources.
